plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.description: Drop JSON rule packs in the plugins folder. Validation rules extend the built-in HL7 checks, FHIR rules the FHIR checks, and anonymization rules the PHI catalogue. No code execution - plugins are pure data.
plugins.noPlugins: No plugins installed. Use the "Open plugins folder" button and create a .json file under validation/, fhir/ or anonymization/.

plugins.stateUnreadable: The saved on/off choices ({file}) could not be read: {error}. Until the file is fixed, each pack follows its own "enabled" setting, so a pack you switched off may be running. The file is left as it is; switching a pack on or off saves new choices and keeps the unreadable file as .state.json.broken (or .state.json.broken.1, .2… when an earlier one is there).

plugins.notice.read_error: the file could not be read ({reason})
plugins.notice.parse_error: the pack's JSON could not be read ({reason})
plugins.notice.no_rules: the pack has no "{key}": it checks nothing
plugins.notice.no_rules_unknown_key: the pack has no "{key}": it checks nothing (unknown key {unknown}: a misspelling?)
plugins.notice.empty_id: the pack has an empty "id": give it one, the pack's on/off switch is saved under it
plugins.notice.empty_name: the pack has an empty "name": Settings shows it as the pack's title
plugins.notice.unknown_severity: unknown severity "{value}", reported as a warning
plugins.notice.field_zero: field 0 is the segment name, not a field (fields count from 1); the rule checks an empty value
plugins.notice.component_zero: component 0 does not exist (components count from 1); component 1 is checked
plugins.notice.fhirpath_invalid: the FHIRPath does not parse ({reason}); the rule reports this on every validation
plugins.notice.not_maskable: not a maskable field (segment name or delimiters); ignored
plugins.notice.segment_malformed: "{segment}" is not a segment name (three letters or digits, such as PID or ZPI); it matches no segment of a well-formed message
plugins.notice.segment_case: segment "{segment}" is read as {key}; write it as {key}
plugins.notice.pattern_too_big: the pattern is too large to compile (over {mb} MB, as a long repetition of \w or \p{L} becomes), so the rule reports this on every validation; a shorter repetition, or an ASCII class such as [A-Za-z0-9_] for \w, is far smaller
plugins.notice.pattern_invalid: the pattern does not compile ({reason}); the rule reports this on every validation
plugins.notice.pattern_heavy: the pattern compiles to over {mb} MB, which slows every load of the pack and takes as much memory; a shorter repetition, or an ASCII class such as [A-Za-z0-9_] for \w, is far smaller

dialog.databaseFallback:
BridgeLab could not open its database, so this time it runs without it:
{path}

Everything works, but nothing of this session is kept when you close BridgeLab: the open tabs (session restore), recent files, the communication history, connection profiles, test cases and preferences. BridgeLab has not deleted or overwritten the file.

Close BridgeLab, deal with the cause given below (a full disk, missing permissions, another program using the file) and start it again. If the file is damaged, move it to another folder: BridgeLab then creates a new, empty one.
dialog.secondInstance:
Another BridgeLab window is already open for your account, and this launch could not hand its files over to it: on Linux that needs a D-Bus session bus.

So that the two windows do not overwrite each other's saved tabs and settings, this one works without the database: nothing of it is kept when you close it.

Work in the other window, or close both and start BridgeLab again.
dialog.recovery:

A recovery copy of them was kept. Restore them now? Either way the copy is then deleted.

comm.ackNoControlId: No Message Control ID (MSH-10) found in the current message — an ACK cannot be correlated.
comm.replyOtherMessage: This ACK acknowledges message control ID {acknowledged}, not {sent} (MSA-2 does not match MSH-10): it does not accept the message sent.
comm.replyUnmatched: This ACK names no message: its MSA-2 is empty, so it cannot be matched to the message sent (MSH-10 {sent}) and does not count as accepting it. A receiver must repeat the sent MSH-10 in MSA-2.

fhirRules.title: FHIR validation rules
fhirRules.intro: Rules run alongside the built-in FHIR checks every time you validate a resource. Each rule is either a FHIRPath expression that must hold, or a path plus a check applied to the values it selects.
fhirRules.none: No rules yet — add one below.
fhirRules.pickOne: Select a rule to edit it.
fhirRules.expressionHint: Evaluated against the resource. The rule fires unless the result is exactly true.
fhirRules.pathHint: The check is applied to every value the selector returns. A selector that returns nothing satisfies every check except “must be present” and cardinality.
fhirRules.messagePlaceholder: Patient must have at least one identifier
fhirRules.testNeedsResource: Open a FHIR resource to test against.
fhirRules.passed: Rule passes on the open resource.
fhirRules.failed: Rule fires on the open resource:
fhirRules.notApplied: The rule did not apply: the open resource is not of that type.
fhirRules.preset.identifierMsg: Patient must have at least one identifier
fhirRules.preset.phoneMsg: Phone number has an unexpected format
fhirRules.preset.cardinalityMsg: Patient must have at least one name
fhirRules.refusal.bad_severity: Rule '{id}': the severity must be error, warning or info.
fhirRules.refusal.bad_pattern: Rule '{id}': the regular expression does not compile ({detail}).
fhirRules.refusal.bad_fhirpath: Rule '{id}': the FHIRPath expression is not valid: {detail}
fhirRules.refusal.path_needs_check: Rule '{id}': a selector needs a check to apply to the values it selects.
fhirRules.refusal.both_forms: Rule '{id}': use either an expression or a selector with a check, not both.
fhirRules.refusal.no_form: Rule '{id}' needs an expression, or a selector with a check.
fhirRules.refusal.duplicate_id: Two rules share the id '{id}': give each rule its own id.
fhirRules.refusal.changed_on_disk: {path} changed on disk after the editor opened it. Nothing was saved: close the editor and open it again to see the current rules.
fhirRules.refusal.invalid_pack: {path} is not a valid rule pack: {detail}
fhirRules.refusal.invalid_pack_unsaved: {path} is not a valid rule pack: {detail}. Nothing was saved: fix the file or move it away, then save again.
fhirRules.refusal.no_resource: The resource to test on is no longer open: open it again, then test.
fhirPackages.title: FHIR profile packages
fhirPackages.intro: The FHIR R4 core is built in, so every resource is checked against its base StructureDefinition: cardinality, element types, choice elements, fixed values, unknown elements. Install implementation guides on top to check the profiles a resource declares in meta.profile.
fhirPackages.whereToGet: Download an implementation guide as a .tgz from packages.fhir.org or your national FHIR registry, then install it here. The R4 core is already built in.
fhirPackages.reloadHint: Read the packages folder again: packages copied there or deleted by hand count without restarting.
fhir.profilesApplied: Checked against the installed FHIR profile packages.

BridgeLab cannot open this file: its name, or the name of a folder on its path, is not valid UTF-8 text (the characters that cannot be read are shown as �). Rename it and open it again.
{path}
file.openedUnparsedKind:
{name} is open as text: {reason}

Fix the text and press F6 to validate it.
file.unparsed.missing_m: the first line starts with “{start}”. Is the M of MSH missing? An HL7 v2 message starts with MSH|^~\&.
file.unparsed.lowercase_header: the first line starts with “{start}”. Segment names are upper case: {header}, not {found}.
file.unparsed.short_header: the {header} segment is too short. After {header} it needs the field separator and the four encoding characters, as in {header}|^~\&.
file.unparsed.bad_delimiters: the {header} segment declares delimiters that cannot be used. After {header} come the field separator and the four encoding characters, five different printable ASCII characters that are not letters, digits or spaces, as in {header}|^~\&.
file.unparsed.no_header: the first line starts with “{start}”, while an HL7 v2 message starts with MSH (FHS or BHS for a batch file). Is there something before the header?
file.unparsed.xml_not_fhir: the file is XML but not a FHIR resource: FHIR XML has a resource such as <Patient> as its root, in the http://hl7.org/fhir namespace.
file.unparsed.invalid_json: the file is not valid JSON:
file.unparsed.json_not_fhir: the file is JSON but not a FHIR resource: it has no "resourceType".
file.unparsed.fhir_invalid: the FHIR resource could not be read:
file.charsetUnsupported: {name} declares the character set {charset} (MSH-18), which BridgeLab cannot decode. It was opened as Windows-1252: names and other text may be wrong, and so may the field boundaries. Do not validate, anonymize or send it before converting it to UTF-8 with another tool.
file.charsetNotUtf8: {name} declares {charset} (MSH-18) but is not valid UTF-8. It was opened as Windows-1252; saving writes it as UTF-8, as it declares.
file.deletedOnDisk: "{name}" was deleted or moved by another program. The tab keeps its text; saving will ask before creating the file again.
file.changedReload: "{name}" was changed by another program. Load the new version?
file.changedReloadDiscard: "{name}" was changed by another program, and this tab has unsaved edits. Load the new version and discard your edits? (Cancel keeps your edits; saving will ask before overwriting.)
file.saveNewer: "{name}" was changed by another program since you opened or last saved it. Overwrite it with this tab?
file.saveRestored: "{name}" was restored with unsaved changes from the last session. Another program may have changed the file since then. Overwrite it with this tab?
file.saveDeleted: "{name}" was deleted or moved since you opened it. Create it again with this tab?
file.notLoaded: "{name}" could not be read from its file, so this tab has no text to save. Reopen the file to edit it.
file.missingAtRestore:
These files were reopened from the last session but are no longer on disk. Their tabs show the text from the session:
{paths}
file.largeConfirm: {name} is {size} MB. A file over {limit} MB can take several GB of memory while it is open, and the window can become slow. Open it anyway?
file.largeRestore: {name} was open when BridgeLab was last closed. It is {size} MB, and a file over {limit} MB can take several GB of memory while it is open. Load it now? If not, its tab stays empty: open the file again to load it.
file.tooLarge: {name} is {size} MB, larger than the {limit} MB BridgeLab can open. Split it into smaller files (a batch file can be cut at its MSH segments) and open those.
paste.tooLarge: The text you are pasting is {size} MB, larger than the {limit} MB BridgeLab can open. Save it to a file and split it into smaller ones (a batch can be cut at its MSH segments).
paste.largeConfirm: The text you are pasting is {size} MB. Text over {limit} MB can take several GB of memory while it is open, and the window can stop answering for a few seconds. Paste it anyway?
file.notRegular:
This is not a regular file (it is a device, a named pipe or a socket), so it cannot be opened:
{path}
file.restoredEmpty:
{reason}

Its tab from the last session was restored without text. Close it, or open the file again once it can be opened.
shortcuts.needsModifier: Use Ctrl or Alt with this key (or F2-F12): on its own it would fire while you type.
shortcuts.needsModifierMac: Use ⌘ or ⌃ with this key (or F2-F12): on its own, or with ⌥ (Option), it would type a character.
shortcuts.editorFixed: An editor key: shown for reference, it cannot be changed here.
status.parseStale: Text does not parse: showing the last version that did
status.parseStaleUnknown: Not recognised as HL7 v2 or FHIR
fp.stale: The editor text does not parse ({reason}). Results come from the last version that did.
bundle.danglingTitle: Dangling reference (target not in the bundle)
bundle.navigateTitle: Click to go to the entry
fp.noResults: No results (the expression returned an empty collection)
fp.hint: Enter a FHIRPath expression and press Enter
fhirRules.status.off: These rules are switched off in Settings → Plugins ("My FHIR rules"): Test still shows what they would do, but validation does not run them until you switch them on.
fhirRules.status.gated: These rules do not run on validation: the Community edition runs a limited number of plugin packs at a time and this one is beyond it (Settings → Plugins).
fhirRules.status.error: The rules file does not load (see Settings → Plugins), so validation does not run these rules.
